events.title: Elixir 1.0 released
events.summary: José Valim released [Elixir] 1.0 on September 18, 2014 — the first stable version on the [Erlang] [BEAM] VM with macros, protocols, and Mix tooling.
events.about: [Elixir] 1.0 committed to stability for production: Phoenix web framework, [OTP] supervision trees, and pipelines for data transformation. Discord, Pinterest, and Bleacher Report adopted it for real-time, fault-tolerant backends.

narrative.whyChosen: [Elixir] 1.0 was the milestone that let teams ship [BEAM]-based systems beyond experiments.
narrative.whyImportant: Stable tooling and semantics unlocked [Elixir] for production web and telecom workloads.
narrative.problemSolved: Pre-1.0 [Elixir] changed too fast for companies to standardize on it.

events.title: iPhone 6 Plus released
events.summary: Apple launched the iPhone 6 Plus on September 19, 2014 — a 5.5-inch phablet with optical image stabilization.
events.about: The Plus legitimized phablets for Western markets and gave developers a 'regular' vs 'plus' size class split that persists in iOS layout APIs. Landscape apps and split views became viable on a phone form factor.

narrative.whyChosen: The 6 Plus made phablets a first-class iOS form factor, not an Android oddity.
narrative.whyImportant: Two iPhone size classes became a permanent constraint for iOS [UI] design.
narrative.problemSolved: Large-screen power users chose Android phablets because Apple offered no equivalent.

events.title: iPhone 6 released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone 6 on September 19, 2014 — jumping to 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch screens after years of 4-inch phones.
events.about: Larger iPhones forced responsive layouts and adaptive [UI] across iOS apps. Reachability, size classes, and split-screen iPad multitasking later built on the bigger canvas the iPhone 6 normalized for mainstream users.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 6 ended Apple's small-phone era and mainstreamed large-screen mobile design.
narrative.whyImportant: Bigger screens changed touch targets, typography, and how developers layout iOS interfaces.
narrative.problemSolved: Four-inch phones cramped content apps; Android phablets were pulling users away.

events.title: Babel transpiler first released
events.summary: Sebastian McKenzie released 6to5 on September 28, 2014 — a JavaScript transpiler that compiled ES6 syntax to ES5 (later renamed Babel).
events.about: Babel lets developers write modern JavaScript — arrow functions, classes, modules — and ship code browsers understand today via build plugins. It powers [React], Vue, and [Node] toolchains through `@babel/preset-env`. Example: write `const greet = () => 'hi'` and Babel outputs `var greet = function () { return 'hi'; }` for older runtimes.

narrative.whyChosen: Babel let the ecosystem adopt new [ECMAScript] features years before engines caught up.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the compiler layer behind every major frontend build pipeline of the 2010s.
narrative.problemSolved: Browsers lagged behind the ES6 spec; teams could not ship modern syntax without manual rewrites.
